Tessa —

Thanks for sending the draft schedule earlier this week. Our procurement team reviewed and attached a clean copy of our preferred changes (see attached Draft-Schedule-VolumeShield-v0.9.docx). Two points where we need your legal team's confirmation before we proceed to signature:

1) The proposed "temporary credit buffer" in Section 4.2 — we'd like that to be an explicit, recoverable credit (applies only to months 1–3 post-migration) rather than a permanent rebate. Can Redwood confirm the mechanism for recovery or true-up?

2) Interaction between the cap/floor language and the dynamic rebate trigger in 5.1 — if usage spikes above the upper collar, we want an automatic rebate; we also want a guarantee that any credits will be applied within the next invoice cycle.

We're OK with a short window for true-up adjustments but need explicit wording that: (a) caps and floors are measured on billed usage (not estimated), and (b) crediting cannot be used to retroactively alter committed volumes for the purpose of discounts.

Attached for reference. Can your team provide a redline that (i) converts the permanent language to a temporary, time-boxed buffer, and (ii) spells out the billing/true-up timing (30/60/90 days options)?

If it's easier, loop legal and finance on your side and we can take a 30-minute call tomorrow.

Appreciate the clear asks and the v0.9. I've looped in finance (Marissa) and legal (Karthik) for text we can ship back. High-level response:

- We can reframe the "temporary credit buffer" as a "rebalancing credit" capped both by duration and quantum. Proposed defaults: 90-day rebalancing window post-migration and cap at 10% of the average monthly invoice during the preceding quarter. Open to adjusting to 30/60 if your accounting team needs faster close.

- Caps/floors: we prefer to keep the measurement on billed usage, not estimates. For clarity we'll add a defined term "Billed Usage" and an explicit statement that credits do not change committed volume bands for the purpose of fee bands.

- Timing: Redwood prefers a 60-day true-up in standard deals (invoice cycle + one month) with an option for accelerated 30-day true-up for enterprise customers. If Borealis requires 30 days, we'll need to set a small administrative fee to cover operational reconciliation (we'll flag that in the redline).

I'm attaching an initial redline (redline_v1.docx) with placeholder language where Legal/Finance want input. Key items we need from you: (i) whether you want a 30/60/90 default, (ii) whether the cap should be % of invoice or a fixed dollar band, and (iii) confirmation that credits can be applied only to future invoices (not refunds).

If you're free today at 3pm PT we can run through the redline. Otherwise we'll iterate over email.

Tessa / Karthik —

Quick finance take after scanning redline_v1: two items to watch from a revenue recognition and billing ops perspective.

1) If we implement a 90-day rebalancing credit that gets applied to future invoices, we must ensure that the credit is recorded as a liability at issuance (ASC 606 impact) and released only when applied. For larger credits (e.g., >$50k) that can materially change ARR, we should require a signed Mutual Action Plan to document intent.

2) Wording that allows credits up to X% of "average monthly invoice" is easier operationally than a fixed dollar amount, but it can be gamed if the baseline quarter is unusually low. Recommend using a 3-month rolling average with an anti-gaming clause ("Baseline Adjustment Event") and an absolute cap floor (e.g., $10k minimum band).

Proposal we should consider adding to redline_v1 (attached as Finance-Impact-notes.pdf):
- Define "Rebalancing Event" with two examples (data migration lag; unexpected spike due to one-time ETL)
- Cap rebalancing credits to the greater of 10% of 3-month rolling average or $10,000, and to be applied within 60 days unless parties agree in writing to extend.

If you want, I can draft the exact markup for the contract language to avoid back-and-forth.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

Team —

I took Marissa's finance notes and Kyle's procurement asks and drafted a legal-ready replacement section for Section 4 (Rebalancing Credits) and Section 5 (Caps and Rebates). Key points in the proposed language (see attached legal-redline.txt):

- "Rebalancing Credit" means a credit issued at Redwood's discretion in response to a documented Rebalancing Event, subject to a cap equal to the greater of (i) 10% of Customer's 3-month rolling average billed usage fee, or (ii) USD 10,000.

- "Rebalancing Event" examples: (a) data migration delay resulting in temporally reduced usage; (b) one-time onboarding spike caused by import/export activity. Each event requires submission of supporting logs within 30 days.

- True-up timing: default 60 days after the month in which the Rebalancing Event is measured. Parties can agree in writing to accelerate to 30 days. Credits apply to future invoices only and are recorded as a contra-liability.

- Caps/floors interaction: Replace term "cap" with "upper fee collar" and clarify that upper fee collar breaches that trigger rebates are measured on Billed Usage per invoice period; credits do not retroactively alter the Customer's committed volume bands or discount band thresholds.

I also added a short carve-out for pilot credits (Section 4.2.b): pilot or sandbox usage credits are not counted against the Rebalancing Credit cap provided both parties mark the usage as "Pilot" in usage records.

I'll paste the proposed contract snippet here so the group can see wording inline: (excerpt)

---
"4.1 Rebalancing Credit. In the event of a Rebalancing Event, Redwood may issue a Rebalancing Credit not to exceed the greater of (i) ten percent (10%) of Customer's aggregate billed usage fee for the three (3) calendar months preceding the month of the Rebalancing Event, and (ii) ten thousand United States Dollars (USD 10,000). Rebalancing Credits shall be evidenced in writing, supported by usage logs, and shall be applied to subsequent invoices in accordance with Section 4.3."

"4.3 True-up Mechanics. Redwood will apply Rebalancing Credits within sixty (60) calendar days of the end of the invoice period in which the Rebalancing Event occurred; provided, however, the parties may agree in writing to an accelerated thirty (30) day schedule. Rebalancing Credits shall not be used to retroactively adjust committed volume bands, discount band calculations, or other fee thresholds."

---

Please review; if we agree to this approach I'll produce a consolidated redline for signature routing. Also recommend we add a short sentence about audit rights for the supporting logs (read-only access to usage reports) to avoid disputes.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: legal-redline.txt (txt)
